summary: An uptime monitor you run yourself: a fetch on an interval with a real timeout, a state machine that only calls a site down after two consecutive failures, one chat message on down and one on recovery, and a public status page with uptime percentages, a latency sparkline and an RSS feed of incidents. Honest about the one thing a single box cannot do: tell your outage from your own network's.

stack.choice: Node 22 with node:http, node:sqlite and global fetch
stack.why: the check is a fetch; the page is a few indexed queries
checks, incidents and monitors in one file

stack.choice: A VPS on a different provider than the sites it watches
stack.why: otherwise it goes down with them

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: A chat webhook URL (Discord, Slack or Telegram)
prerequisites.why: Alerts go to a chat channel you already watch. A webhook URL is the only credential this needs.
prerequisites.get: Discord: Server settings > Integrations > Webhooks > New Webhook, copy the URL. Slack: create an app at api.slack.com/apps, enable Incoming Webhooks, add to a channel, copy the URL. Telegram: create a bot with @BotFather and use the bot token plus your chat id.
prerequisites.verify: curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"content":"test"}' <url> posts a message (Discord form; Slack uses a text field)

prerequisites.name: The URLs to watch, with what healthy means for each
prerequisites.why: Each monitor needs a URL, an interval, an expected status and optionally a keyword the body must contain.
prerequisites.get: List every site or endpoint. For each decide: check every 60 seconds or 300, expect 200, and a word that only appears when the page really works.

prerequisites.name: A small VPS on a different provider than your sites
prerequisites.why: A monitor hosted next to what it watches reports nothing when that host dies. Different provider, ideally a different region.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner if your sites are elsewhere, or vice versa. Smallest Ubuntu 24.04 instance with SSH.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: A status page address you can give people, e.g. status.yourdomain.com.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: PORT
env.where: Any free port; Caddy proxies to it.

env.name: ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL
env.where: The chat webhook from the prerequisites.

env.name: FAILURES_BEFORE_DOWN
env.where: Consecutive failures before a monitor is called down.

env.name: RETENTION_DAYS
env.where: Days of raw checks to keep. Incidents are kept forever.

env.name: SITE_URL
env.where: Public base URL for the status page and RSS feed.

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

phases.title: The check
phases.goal: One function from a monitor to a result, with a timeout that actually fires and distinct error kinds.

steps.do: Create the project and the three tables
steps.detail: monitors (id, name, url, interval_seconds, timeout_ms, expected_status, keyword, enabled, status, consecutive_failures, last_checked_at, last_change_at), checks (id, monitor_id, checked_at, ok, status_code, latency_ms, error), incidents (id, monitor_id, started_at, ended_at, cause). Index checks(monitor_id, checked_at).
commands: mkdir uptime && cd uptime && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.detail: fetch with an AbortController timeout, follow redirects, read at most 64 kB of body for the keyword, record latency. Return ok plus one of: dns, tls, timeout, status, keyword, as the error.

steps.do: Add a CLI to run one check by hand

check: A good URL records ok with a sane latency
A URL that never responds fails at the timeout, not later
A 404 against expected 200 fails with the code recorded
A keyword monitor fails when the word is absent from a 200 body

phases.title: Scheduler
phases.goal: Each monitor on its own interval, concurrently with a cap, and one bad monitor never stops the loop.

steps.detail: Every 5 seconds find monitors due (last_checked_at plus interval before now), run up to 10 concurrently, catch every exception per monitor. On boot treat every monitor as due.

steps.do: Store a checks row per run and update the monitor's last_checked_at

check: Monitors at 30, 60 and 300 seconds keep their cadence over ten minutes
A monitor pointed at a hanging host does not delay the others
A thrown exception inside one check leaves the loop running

phases.title: Transitions and incidents
phases.goal: Down only after N consecutive failures, up on the first success, one incident per outage.

steps.detail: Increment consecutive_failures on a failed check; at FAILURES_BEFORE_DOWN flip to down. Any success resets the counter and flips to up.

steps.do: Open and close incidents on the transitions
steps.detail: Open a row on the flip to down with the first failure's error as cause; set ended_at on recovery. Incidents, not checks, are what people read later.

check: A single blip opens no incident
Two consecutive failures open one
Recovery closes it with a correct duration
Flapping up/down/up/down produces one incident, not four

phases.title: Alerting
phases.goal: One message down, one up, retries that never stall the loop.

steps.detail: Down: monitor name and the error. Three retries with backoff, then record the failure and move on.

steps.do: Send the recovery message with the outage duration
steps.detail: Duration comes from the incident row's started_at and ended_at.

check: Taking a site down produces exactly one message
Keeping it down produces none
Recovery produces exactly one with the duration
A webhook URL that 500s does not stall checking

phases.title: Status page
phases.goal: A public page whose numbers can be argued with, and a feed people can subscribe to.

steps.detail: One row per monitor: dot, state, uptime over 24 h, 7 d and 30 d with the denominator printed (over 2,880 checks), a latency sparkline as inline SVG, recent incidents with durations. Meta refresh every 30 seconds.

steps.do: Add /status.rss with one item per incident
Seed 90 days of checks and time the page

check: Percentages match a hand-written query
The page renders with zero history on a fresh install
It loads in under 200 ms with 90 days of checks
The RSS feed validates

phases.title: Retention and deploy
phases.goal: Old checks pruned, incidents kept, live behind HTTPS on the other provider.

steps.do: Nightly prune of checks older than RETENTION_DAYS, never incidents
Add /healthz, systemd with restart-on-failure, Caddy, and the README
steps.detail: README: the single-region caveat stated plainly, the instruction to host on a different provider than the things watched, and the RSS URL.

check: Pruning does not distort the 30-day figure
The service survives a reboot with state intact
The status page states the single-region caveat

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the monitor is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A status page you could show customers: honest percentages, incident history, a feed, and a monitor that is itself monitored from a third place.

architecture.swap: Add a TCP or DNS checker as another function with the same result shape

architecture.owns: the due loop and concurrency cap
architecture.swap: Pure orchestration; unchanged by new checker types
Tunable by FAILURES_BEFORE_DOWN; testable with a fake clock
Any UI over checks and incidents

operations.backup: SQLite .backup nightly. Incidents are the history worth keeping.
operations.restore: Copy back, start, confirm monitors resume and the incident list is intact.
operations.monitoring: Watch the watcher: an external check from a third provider on /healthz.
operations.incident: If the monitor is down the sites are unwatched, not down. Restore, then review the gap by hand.

releaseGate: Runs on a different provider than any monitored site
One restore drill performed and dated
Status page loads under 200 ms with 90 days of data

notIncluded: Multi-region probes. One box cannot tell an outage from its own bad network; the status page says so.
Subscriber email notifications, incident templates, on-call.
after: A second probe location that must agree before an incident opens
